quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should not be used unless the roadway is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or in addition to turn signals. When your left arm is extended straight out to the side, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: To apply the front brake, squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure firmly and smoothly, increasing pressure gradually.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight only if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times, even during the day. This makes you twice as likely to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: To protect yourself while riding, pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely enough to flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some leg.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or heavy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Your clothing should fit snugly without flapping in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who do not have much experience riding their motorcycle.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Takes away your ability to change direction.
Is only a problem if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes away your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash and injury. When the rear wheel locks up from too much brake pressure, you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and brightly colored clothing when riding. Crashes happen at any time of day or night, so stay visible whenever you ride.

questions.question: Curved mirrors make cars seem:
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors, but they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Use your high beam headlight, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following provides good protection for a motorcyclist?

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Choose boots or shoes with low heels that cover your ankles. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: A driver on an entrance ramp may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter traffic safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if it is safe to do so. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give the merging driver space.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is located at the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn toward where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn toward where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to increase your visibility.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should you tell them?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Mount the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mount the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger complete safety instructions. Ask them to get on the motorcycle only after the engine is started. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when the motorcycle is stopped.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. A mirror may show a little of your arm or shoulder, but focus on seeing the road behind and to the side.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and pass it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and pass it.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it calmly. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. Shifting to a lower gear will slow you down.

questions.question: When you approach an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your leg joints absorb the impact. This keeps you from being thrown off the motorcycle.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire go flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is the most common sign of tire failure.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.
